title: Landsman Voted to Stop Insider Trading and Voter Suppression
text:
Landsman Voted to Stop Insider Trading and Voter Suppression
Cincinnati, OH – Today, Congressman Greg Landsman (D-OH-01) released the following statement after voting against Congressional Republicans’ Stop Insider Trading Act:
I voted to stop voter suppression and insider trading. This bill had two purposes: make it harder for Americans to vote and codify insider trading in Congress.
The bill includes aspects of Trump’s voter suppression bill the “SAVE America Act,” which will prevent tens of millions of Americans from voting. If Americans do not have the exact photo ID spelled out in the bill, they cannot vote.
In addition to the voter suppression language, the bill codifies stock trading in Congress. The bill allows members to continue owning individual stocks. It allows members to continue selling individual stocks. It even allows members to continue buying stocks in certain circumstances.
Congress must ban members from owning, buying, or selling any individual stock while in office. No loopholes, no exceptions.
I supported an amendment to replace this bill with the Restore Trust in Government Act, which actually bans members of Congress from owning, buying, or selling stocks.
Public trust in our government is at an all-time low. Every member of Congress should want to be part of the generation that earns this trust back.
BACKGROUND
Landsman is one of the few Members of Congress to sell all his individual stocks. He has also introduced two bills this Congress to ban members of Congress, their spouses, and dependents from owning or trading stocks – the No Profiting off Public Service Act and the Drain the Swamp Act.
###
